messages.subject: Points in polygons ggmap
parts:
The script below draws a polygon over a world map. It’s reproducible – you should be able to copy/paste to see how this is done. Using over() from the sp package, I can then easily find the number of points which lie in each polygon drawn.

coordsX = c(76.7864778,  -3.1111604,   1.0029375, 109.7523700,  79.0270900,  18.2920100,  -5.0525788,  -9.4254852,   0.1314163,
34.9690523)
coordsY = c(13.8176899, -32.7283195,  12.9977900,   0.4631664,  25.1343479,  13.8666859,  57.5056500,  53.8051547,  54.7481300,
57.7765223)
myCoords = data.frame(coordsX,coordsY)

library(sp)
coordinates(myCoords) <- c('coordsX', 'coordsY') 
plot(myCoords)
crs.geo <- CRS("+proj=longlat +ellps=WGS84 +datum=WGS84") # define projection
proj4string(myCoords) <- crs.geo 
plot(myCoords, pch=20, col="steelblue")

library(maptools)
data(wrld_simpl)
plot(wrld_simpl, add=T)

library(dismo)
mypolygon <- drawPoly()    # click on the map to draw a polygon and press ESC
proj4string(mypolygon) <- crs.geo

My question  is – can I draw polygons in the same way using a function in the ggmap package?
